Consumer complaint narrative:
To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding an improperly reported charged-off credit card account furnished by Bank of America , which reflects a cancellation of debt but continues to be reported as an outstanding obligation on my consumer credit reports. 

This complaint concerns violations of federal tax law, the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), and applicable credit reporting standards. 

Account Information Creditor : Bank of America Account XXXX : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  ( ending as reported ) Account Type : Credit Card Date Opened : XX/XX/XXXX Closed Date : XX/XX/XXXX Balance Reported : {$11000.00} High Balance : {$13000.00} Bureaus Reporting : XXXX, XXXX, XXXX  Admission of Cancellation-of-Debt Event This tradeline is reported using explicit cancellation language, including : Canceled by credit grantor Charged off as bad debt Unpaid balance reported as a loss by the credit grantor These statements constitute an identifiable cancellation-of-debt event under : 26 U.S.C. 6050P Treasury Regulation 1.6050P-1 Federal law requires that when a creditor cancels or discharges indebtedness of {$600.00} or more, the creditor must issue IRS Form 1099-C to the consumer and the Internal Revenue Service. 

To date : No IRS Form 1099-C has been issued or provided No explanation has been offered as to why this debt is treated as canceled for accounting purposes but not reported as canceled for tax purposes Inaccurate and Misleading Credit Reporting ( FCRA Violations ) A creditor can not lawfully report a debt as canceled or written off while simultaneously reporting it as a collectible or enforceable obligation on a consumer credit report. 

This constitutes inaccurate and misleading reporting in violation of : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Furnishers may not report information they know or have reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate or misleading.

15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Requires a reasonable investigation and verification of the legal status of the debt once disputed. 

By continuing to report this account without issuing the required tax documentation or clearly identifying the debt as canceled, Bank of America is furnishing materially misleading information to consumer reporting agencies. 

Demand for Relief I hereby demand that Bank of America : Immediately delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies due to inaccurate and misleading reporting. 

Provide a copy of the IRS Form 1099-C issued for this account ; or Provide written confirmation that no cancellation-of-debt event occurred, including the legal basis for reporting the debt as canceled by credit grantor ; Absent production of the required documentation, continued reporting constitutes willful noncompliance with federal law. 

This complaint is being submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) for regulatory review and enforcement. 

Please provide a written response within the CFPBs required response timeframe.

I submitted a {$510.00} payment by check to an auto loan servicer on behalf of another individual. The auto loan is not in my name. I made the payment as a third party to satisfy a required monthly payment connected to a court-ordered obligation requiring the vehicle to be retained and payments made. 

The company cashed my check, which constitutes acceptance of the payment. 

After accepting the payment, the company improperly issued a refund instead of correctly applying the payment. The refund check was mailed to a financial technology company that does not accept physical checks. That company has confirmed in writing that the check was rejected and returned to the loan servicer. 

Despite the refund being returned, I was informed that the loan servicer intends to redirect my funds to a third party, even though I am the original payer and there is no authorization or court order allowing my money to be released to anyone else. 

In addition, the loan servicer has initiated repossession activity, claiming nonpayment. This alleged nonpayment exists only because the company failed to properly apply an accepted third-party payment and mishandled the refund. The delinquency and repossession activity are the direct result of the companys internal processing errors, not a failure to pay. 

This has created a false delinquency, interfered with compliance with a court order, and caused immediate and ongoing harm through wrongful repossession activity.

Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this complaint to formally dispute multiple fraudulent accounts that have been opened in my name without my authorization. I did not open, authorize, or benefit from these accounts. I believe I am a victim of identity theft. 

These accounts and the associated debts are inaccurate and must be investigated and removed in accordance with federal law.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., I have the right to dispute inaccurate information on my credit report, and consumer reporting agencies and furnishers are required to conduct a reasonable investigation and correct or delete unverifiable or fraudulent information. 
Additionally, under the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act ( FACTA ), I have the right to block fraudulent information resulting from identity theft once proper documentation is provided.

If any third-party debt collectors are involved, the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq., prohibits the collection of debts that are not valid and requires debt validation upon dispute.

Consumer complaint narrative:
To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint against Bank of America for continuing to report a charged-off credit card account that the creditor itself has identified as canceled, without issuing the legally required IRS Form 1099-C, and while furnishing inaccurate and misleading information to consumer reporting agencies. 

This complaint concerns violations of 26 U.S.C. 6050P, Treasury Regulation 1.6050P-1, and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ).

Account Information Creditor : Bank of America Account Number : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  ( as reported ) Account Type : Credit Card Date Opened : XX/XX/XXXX Closed Date : XX/XX/XXXX Balance Reported : {$12000.00} High Balance : {$13000.00} Bureaus Reporting : TransUnion, Experian, Equifax Creditors Admission of Debt Cancellation This tradeline contains explicit cancellation language, including : Canceled by credit grantor Charged off as bad debt Unpaid balance reported as a loss by the credit grantor These statements constitute an identifiable cancellation-of-debt event under : 26 U.S.C. 6050P ( a ) Treasury Regulation 1.6050P-1 ( b ) ( XXXX ) Federal law requires that when a creditor cancels or discharges {$600.00} or more of indebtedness, the creditor must issue IRS Form 1099-C to both the consumer and the Internal Revenue Service. 

To date : No Form 1099-C has been issued or provided to me No explanation has been given as to why Bank of America reports the debt as canceled while failing to comply with federal tax-reporting requirements Inaccurate and Misleading Credit Reporting ( FCRA Violations ) A creditor can not lawfully treat a debt as canceled for accounting purposes while simultaneously reporting it as an active derogatory obligation on a consumer credit report. 

This constitutes inaccurate and misleading furnishing in violation of : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Prohibits furnishing information that is inaccurate or materially misleading. 

15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Requires a reasonable investigation and verification of the legal status of the debt after dispute. 

By continuing to report this tradeline without issuing the required IRS documentation or clarifying the legal status of the obligation, Bank of America is furnishing information that misrepresents whether the debt is still owed. 

Demand for Relief I hereby demand that Bank of America : Immediately delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies due to inaccurate and misleading reporting. 

Provide a copy of the IRS Form 1099-C issued for this account ; or Provide written confirmation that no cancellation-of-debt event occurred, including the legal basis for reporting the account as canceled by credit grantor ; or Absent production of the required documentation, continued reporting constitutes willful noncompliance with federal law. 

This complaint is being submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) for regulatory review and enforcement. 

Please provide a written response within the CFPB-mandated response timeframe.

Consumer complaint narrative:
To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding a charged-off credit card account reported by Bank of America that reflects an admitted cancellation of debt, yet continues to be reported as an outstanding derogatory tradeline on my consumer credit reports.

This complaint concerns violations of federal tax law, the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), and applicable credit reporting standards. 

Account Information Creditor : Bank of America Account Number : * * * * ( as reported ) Account Type : Credit Card Date Opened : XX/XX/XXXX Closed Date : XX/XX/XXXX Balance Reported : {$11000.00} High Balance : {$13000.00} Bureaus Reporting : XXXX XXXX XXXX Admission of Cancellation-of-Debt Event This tradeline is reported using explicit cancellation language, including : Canceled by credit grantor Charged off as bad debt Unpaid balance reported as a loss by the credit grantor These statements constitute an identifiable cancellation-of-debt event under : 26 U.S.C. 6050P Treasury Regulation 1.6050P-1 Federal law requires that when a creditor cancels or discharges indebtedness of {$600.00} or more, the creditor must issue IRS Form 1099-C to the consumer and the Internal Revenue Service. 

To date : No IRS Form 1099-C has been issued or provided to me No explanation has been offered justifying why this debt is treated as canceled for accounting purposes but not reported as canceled for tax purposes Inaccurate and Misleading Credit Reporting ( FCRA Violations ) A creditor can not lawfully report a debt as canceled or written off while simultaneously reporting it as a collectible or enforceable obligation on a consumer credit report. 

This constitutes inaccurate and misleading reporting in violation of : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Furnishers may not report information they know or have reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate or misleading.

15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Requires a reasonable investigation and verification of the legal status of the debt once disputed.

By continuing to report this account without issuing the required IRS documentation or clearly identifying the debt as canceled, Bank of America is furnishing materially misleading information to consumer reporting agencies. 

Demand for Relief I hereby demand that Bank of America : Provide a copy of the IRS Form 1099-C issued for this account ; Immediately delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies due to inaccurate and misleading reporting. 

Provide written confirmation that no cancellation-of-debt event occurred, including the legal basis for reporting the account as canceled by credit grantor ; or Absent production of the required documentation, continued reporting constitutes willful noncompliance with federal law. 

This complaint is being submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) for regulatory review and enforcement. 

Please provide a written response within the CFPBs required response timeframe.

My personal identifying information was exposed in the XXXX  data breach, which included my name, Social Security number, date of birth, and address.

As a direct and foreseeable result of this breach, accounts that I never opened, authorized, or consented to have appeared on my credit report. I am a verified victim of identity theft, and these accounts are not mine. 
Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ( FCRA 605B ), identity-theft-related information must be blocked and deleted immediately once notice is received. Continued reporting after notice constitutes willful non-compliance.

II. FRAUDULENT COLLECTION ACCOUNT SEQUIUM ASSET SOLUTIONS, L I am disputing a fraudulent collection account currently being reported by Sequium Asset SolutionsXXXX XXXX originally associated with XXXX , which has been sold from one debt collector to another without my consent or authorization.

The original debt collector previously deleted this account, establishing that the debt was fraudulent and unverifiable.

Despite this, the same alleged debt has been resold and re-reported, which is outrageous, abusive, and unlawful.

I never consented to the use of my personal information, never entered into any contract, and never authorized any creditor or debt collector to collect on this alleged account.

This repeated resale of the same unverified debt is materially harming my creditworthiness and violates federal consumer protection laws.

III. DEBT VALIDATION DEMAND FDCPA 1692g Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1692g, I am formally demanding full debt validation. You are required to provide the following : A complete, itemized payment history from account origination The original contract or application bearing my legal wet signature Proof I agreed to and authorized this alleged debt Disclosure of any insurance claim, bond claim, or tax write-off filed The complete chain of title, including all assignments, transfers, and proof of lawful custody granting authority to collect Absent this documentation, the alleged debt is unenforceable and must be deleted immediately.

Consumer complaint narrative: I have had a Chime bank account since XXXX and had never had any problems until XXXX and XXXX of XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX I unfortunately was XXXX and did not get out until XX/XX/XXXX. Upon release I wanted access to my Chime bank account again but I discovered that I was unable to get back in on my own. On XX/XX/XXXX I called Chime customer service and attempted to regain access to my account and was told that I needed to send a copy of my ID in order to verify my identity and gain access to my account again, I didn't have an ID at the time so I couldn't get into the account. I finally got my ID back and I called Chime customer service again on XX/XX/XXXX and ended up gaining access to my account that day and I spoke to someone from Chime three different times that day. While I was still on the phone with a customer service representative I realized that my checking account had a balance of - {$370.00} and I told this to the guy I was on the phone with, saying that I hadn't used the account for about 27 months and how could that be? I looked at the transaction record and saw that there were several pay anyone transfers in and out of my account that I had not authorized and had no knowledge of starting on XX/XX/XXXX up until XX/XX/XXXX, ending with three different transfer adjustments totaling {$390.00}. The last transaction before these pay anyone transfers started on XX/XX/XXXX was from XX/XX/XXXX and it was a declined payment for {$10.00}, I also had no income being deposited into this account when I was incarcerated. The dispute I filed on XX/XX/XXXX was denied sometime around XX/XX/XXXX and I didn't really get a straight answer as to why it was denied, I was passed around from department to department for an hour and 40 minutes until I was finally told that I could appeal the decision, which I did, and the appeal was also denied. I tried to close the account because they completely upset me and they said I couldn't until the outstanding balance was repaid. The only evidence that I was able to provide for the dispute process was a paper showing that I had been convicted to serve 2 years in the department of corrections in my state and I included my prison ID, because that was all that I had to even halfway try to prove anything. Any other evidence there was I felt that they had it right in front of them, starting with me having been a customer for five years with no issues, my transaction record, if they kept call logs they could see that I had just regained access to the account a month after the fraudulent transfers were made. Lastly, I truly can't understand how Chime allowed my account to be overdrawn or adjusted to the point where I am {$370.00} in the negative.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Re : Deceptive Marketing and Interface Design ( " Dark Patterns '' ) Regarding Chase Sapphire Reserve Hotel Benefit Complainant Context : I have been a Chase Sapphire Reserve cardholder for 8 years. I am also an attorney, and I state this to emphasize that I am a sophisticated consumer accustomed to analyzing complex terms. Despite my professional background and diligence, I was misled by Chases booking platform design, suggesting that this practice is intended to deceive the average consumer. 

The Issue : In late 2025, Chase increased the annual fee for the XXXX XXXX card, justifying the hike with " added benefits, '' specifically a {$250.00} statement credit for " The Edit '' hotel bookings. 

Despite booking a two night stay at a qualifying hotel, the XXXX XXXX in XXXX, per the terms and conditions, I was denied this credit. Chases refusal to honor the benefit relies on a deceptive three-part architecture : XXXX. Ambiguous Definition of " Prepaid Booking '' : Chases promotional language for this benefit explicitly states : " Get up to {$250.00} in statement credits through XXXX for prepaid bookings made with The Edit. '' This language is materially ambiguous. To a reasonable consumer, " prepaid '' simply distinguishes a booking paid in advance from XXXX paid at the hotel counter. It does not inherently distinguish between payment methods ( cash vs. points ). Since a points redemption is a full payment made in advance, it fits the plain-language definition of a " prepaid booking. '' Chase relies on an undisclosed, narrower definition to deny the benefit. 

2. Exacerbation via Interface Design ( " Dark Patterns '' ) : Closed Ecosystem : " The Edit '' is a specific collection of hotels that can only be booked through Chase 's proprietary portal.

Points as Currency : Chase markets Ultimate Rewards points as a currency intrinsic to the Reserve account, effectively valuing them at 1.5 cents per point for travel.

The Trap : Because the portal, the hotel collection, and the currency ( points ) are all parts of the Reserve ecosystem, it is reasonable to conclude that any booking made within this system constitutes a booking made with your Chase Reserve.

3. Failure to Warn : Within the Chase Travel portal " Pay with Points '' is the default option, effectively steering customers into a non-qualifying transaction structure. Nowhere in the promotional material or the immediate checkout flow does Chase disclose that accepting the default payment method ( " Pay with Points '' ) disqualifies the user from the advertised {$250.00} credit.

I contacted Chase via phone, and explained the issue at hand, and they refused to help. I spoke with several supervisors in several different departments and none of them were able to provide a resolution to my issue. Some of the customer service reps even admitted that I was not the first person to have this issue and they have been receiving complaints regarding this benefit.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am submitting this as a new complaint and formal reinvestigation demand, as the previous case ( # XXXX ) was closed without resolution of the underlying issue. The inaccurate reporting remains on my credit file, and I do not accept the prior closure as a final determination. 

This letter serves as formal notice that the accounts reported by : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

are fraudulent and do not belong to me. 

I did not open, authorize, apply for, or agree to these accounts. These accounts are the result of identity theft. 

Experian Fraud Determination I was formally informed by Experian that the XXXX and XXXX accounts were determined to be fraudulent. Experian recognized that the tradelines were the result of identity theft. 

Despite this, the accounts continue to be reported or handled improperly by other reporting agencies. 

The fact that XXXX major consumer reporting agency has already recognized these accounts as fraud demonstrates that the underlying data is unreliable and that continued reporting by others is unreasonable. 

FTC Identity Theft Report Filed I have filed an official Identity Theft Report with the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) documenting that these accounts were opened fraudulently using my personal identifying information. 

The FTC report was completed truthfully and under penalty of perjury. 

This is not a casual dispute. 
This is not a billing disagreement. 
This is a documented identity theft claim. 

Closure of Prior Case Was Procedural, Not Substantive The previous case ( # XXXX ) was closed, but the inaccurate reporting remains. Closing a complaint without correcting the underlying inaccuracy does not resolve the issue. 

The accounts still appear as derogatory collections and continue to : Lower my credit score Misrepresent my creditworthiness Influence lending decisions Cause ongoing financial harm Because the reporting persists, this matter remains unresolved. 

Demand for Method of Verification If the accounts are being maintained as valid, I am demanding full disclosure of the method of verification used, including : The specific documents reviewed Whether verification was conducted electronically through e-OSCAR The name and title of the individual who verified the account The date and system used for verification The chain of custody of the alleged account data Simply stating that the furnisher verified the account is insufficient. 

Verification of data is not verification of ownership. 

Demand for Contractual Proof If Nationwide or Aargon contend that the accounts are legitimate, they must produce competent proof of authorization, including : A signed contract bearing my wet signature ; or A verifiable electronic signature showing affirmative consent ; and Authentication logs tied to account opening ; and Application records initiated by me To date, no signed agreement or authenticated proof has been produced. 

Address association does not equal consent. 
Residency does not equal contract. 
Data presence does not equal authorization. 

Without contractual documentation, continued reporting is improper. 

Improper Reliance on Furnisher Statements Merely contacting the furnisher and accepting their statement that the account is valid does not constitute a reasonable reinvestigation in an identity theft case. 

When fraud is alleged and supported by an FTC affidavit, a reporting agency must do more than forward the dispute and accept the response at face value. 

The issue is ownership. 

If the furnisher can not prove I entered into a contractual relationship, the account must be deleted. 

Continued Reporting Causes Harm The continued presence of these fraudulent accounts has caused substantial harm, including : Credit score damage Increased interest rates Reduced credit access Emotional distress Time and expense disputing inaccurate reporting I should not suffer financial consequences for fraud committed by someone else. 

Failure to Block Fraudulent Information When a consumer submits an identity theft report, fraudulent accounts must be blocked from reporting unless the furnisher establishes that the information is correct and belongs to the consumer. 

No such proof has been provided. 

Therefore, continued reporting is improper. 

Formal Requests I am formally requesting : Immediate deletion and blocking of the XXXX XXXX XXXX tradeline. 

Immediate deletion and blocking of the XXXX XXXX tradeline. 

Written confirmation of deletion. 

Written confirmation that these accounts will not be reinserted. 

Full disclosure of the method of verification used. 

Copies of any signed agreements relied upon to maintain reporting. 

If signed contracts or authenticated proof can not be produced, deletion is required. 

This Is a Stall and Escalation Notice This letter serves as notice that the matter remains open and under active dispute. 

Any continued reporting without production of signed contractual proof will be considered reporting without proper validation. 

I am creating this new case because the prior closure did not correct the inaccuracy. 

The accounts remain fraudulent. 

The reporting remains harmful. 

The matter remains unresolved. 

Final Position I did not open these accounts. 
I did not authorize these accounts. 
Experian has already recognized them as fraud. 
I filed an FTC Identity Theft Report. 

If the furnishers can not produce competent proof of authorization, the accounts must be permanently deleted. 

Until that occurs, this dispute remains active.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am submitting this complaint regarding inaccurate credit reporting by my student loan servicer and the continued failure to correct clearly documented errors despite repeated disputes over several years. 

In XXXX, my student loans were placed in an approved forbearance status. Despite this, multiple late payments were reported to the credit bureaus during that same period. Late payments reported while an account is in an approved forbearance are inaccurate and misleading. 

Over the past XXXX years, I have repeatedly contacted the loan servicing center and requested correction of these late payments. I provided documentation confirming the forbearance status, including copies sent approximately XXXX years ago. For the last XXXX years, I have continued to follow up and formally request that the late payments be corrected to reflect the account as current during the forbearance period in XXXX. Despite these efforts, the inaccurate reporting remains. 

This ongoing failure to correct inaccurate information is causing substantial financial harm and emotional distress to me and my daughter. As a single parent, my creditworthiness directly affects my ability to secure housing, financing, and maintain financial stability for my family. 

I am invoking my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681, as follows : Under FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), a furnisher of information may not report information that it knows or has reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate. Reporting late payments during an approved forbearance period constitutes inaccurate reporting. 

Under FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 8 ), furnishers are required to conduct a reasonable investigation of disputes submitted directly by consumers. I have submitted multiple disputes and supporting documentation, yet the inaccurate reporting continues.

Under FCRA 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ), consumer reporting agencies are required to conduct a reasonable investigation of disputed information. Repeated verification of information that conflicts with documented forbearance records raises serious concerns about the adequacy of these investigations.

Under FCRA 607 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ), consumer reporting agencies must follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of the information reported. Reporting late payments during a confirmed forbearance period fails to meet this standard. 

Additionally, to the extent any accommodations or payment relief programs were in effect, federal guidance and industry standards require accurate reporting of accounts in forbearance and prohibit misleading delinquency reporting during approved relief periods. 

Despite being placed on notice repeatedly, the servicer has failed to correct the reporting, and the credit bureaus have continued to publish this inaccurate information. 

I am requesting the following resolution : Immediate removal or correction of all late payments reported during the XXXX  forbearance period. 

Updating of the account history to accurately reflect the account as current or in forbearance during that time. 

Written confirmation that corrections have been submitted to all credit reporting agencies.

Consumer complaint narrative:
CFPB COMPLAINT XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Product : Retail Installment Sales Contract Vehicle : XXXX  XXXX XXXX Date of Execution : XX/XX/year> This complaint concerns material disclosure defects at consummation, post-execution alteration of credit disclosures, and coordinated enforcement of a contract whose operative terms remain unclear. 

On XX/XX/year>, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX presented and executed a Retail Installment Sales Contract in connection with the above-referenced vehicle. That contract was subsequently assigned to Ally Financial. 

Ally Financial has acknowledged in writing that the contract originated by XXXX XXXX contained omitted or incorrectly stated material disclosures and that corrected disclosures were generated on XX/XX/year> sixteen ( 16 ) days after execution. 

This admission establishes that the contract as originated was not accurate and complete at consummation. 

Under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and Regulation Z, material disclosures must be accurate and complete at consummation. Post-consummation generation of corrected disclosures reflects a disclosure defect at origination, not a clerical adjustment. 

I was never provided with a corrected contract dated XX/XX/year>. 
I did not sign or authorize any amended agreement on that date. 
I did not execute or ratify any post-consummation modification. 

Despite this, the transaction continues to be enforced as fully valid without re-execution or documented mutual assent. 

Regulatory Concerns This matter raises the following compliance concerns : Origination of a contract containing omitted or incorrectly stated material disclosures. 
Post-consummation generation of corrected disclosures without consumer re-execution. 
Absence of documented assent to any amended instrument. 
Assignment of a contract requiring correction without clear identification of the operative agreement. 
Continued enforcement and credit reporting under contractual ambiguity. 

I have formally requested : Identification of the operative contract XXXX XXXX asserts governs this account. 
A complete copy of any corrected or amended agreement dated XX/XX/year>. 
Documentation bearing my signature reflecting assent to any amended terms. 
A full breakdown of bundled products and third-party payees. 
Funding documentation demonstrating disbursement consistent with the executed agreement. 

To date, XXXX XXXX has not produced a contract bearing my signature dated XX/XX/year> and has not clearly identified which agreement governs. 

Coordinated Enforcement and Assignee Risk The originating dealer and the assignee lender are presently aligned in enforcing a credit obligation despite acknowledged post-execution corrections and the absence of any signed amended instrument. 

Under TILA, assignees may be subject to liability for disclosure violations apparent on the face of assigned documents. Where a contract required post-consummation correction of material disclosures, questions arise as to whether the defect was apparent at assignment and whether continued enforcement is appropriate without re-execution. 

Neither XXXX XXXX nor Ally has clearly stated whether : The XX/XX/year> contract governs despite acknowledged disclosure defects ; or A XX/XX/year> corrected version governs despite the absence of consumer assent. 

If the XX/XX/XXXX contract was compliant, correction would not have been required. 
If correction was required, enforcement without documented mutual assent creates material compliance exposure for both originator and assignee. 

Appropriate Compliance Resolution Where a retail installment contract required post-consummation correction of material disclosures and no amended instrument was executed, the most efficient compliance remedy is not continued enforcement under ambiguity. 

The appropriate resolution may include : Formal re-execution with full and documented consumer consent ; or Repurchase of the contract by the originating dealer and unwind of the assignment ; or Written confirmation that no obligation will be enforced based on terms not provided to or agreed to at consummation. 

Repurchase or unwind would resolve assignment ambiguity, eliminate potential assignee liability exposure, and allow corrective action at the origination level without prolonged regulatory scrutiny. 

Resolution Requested 1. Written identification of the operative contract governing this account. 
2. Delivery of any corrected disclosures XXXX XXXX and/or Ally rely upon. 
3. Documentation bearing my signature for any amended instrument dated XX/XX/year>. 
4. Written confirmation that no obligation will be enforced based on terms never provided to or agreed to at consummation. 
5. If no signed corrected instrument exists, repurchase and unwind of the assigned contract as the appropriate compliance resolution. 
6. Correction of any adverse credit reporting tied to disputed or non-consensual contractual terms. 
7. Confirmation that XXXX XXXX has reviewed its origination and post-consummation correction procedures to ensure compliance with TILA and Regulation Z. 

This complaint concerns disclosure compliance at consummation, proper contract formation, assignment responsibility, and enforcement integrity. I respectfully request formal regulatory review of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  origination and assignment practices in connection with this transaction.
